content: There are two types of lists that can be created: unordered bullet lists and ordered numbered lists. Bullet lists are characterized by a blue square preceding the text, while numbered lists assign a specific order or number to each item. To create a bullet list, begin each line with an asterisk symbol (). For example, typing the following: ``` This is a list This is part of the same list As is this. ``` will produce: This is a list This is part of the same list As is this. To create a numbered list, start each line with a hash symbol (). For instance, typing: ``` I'm number one. I'm number two. I'm number three. ``` will yield: 1. I'm number one. 2. I'm number two. 3. I'm number three. It is important to note that a list ends when a line without the list character (e.g., or ) is encountered. Additionally, numbering restarts at 1 when a new hash symbol () is used. For example: ``` List 1 List 1 No List List 2 ``` produces: 1. List 1 2. List 1 No List 1. List 2 To create multi-leveled lists, simply add an additional list character at the beginning of the line to indicate a new level. For example: ``` List Level 1 List Level 2 List Level 3 List Level 2 List Level 1 ``` results in: List Level 1 List Level 2 List Level 3 List Level 2 List Level 1 This method works for both bullet and numbered lists. For instance: ``` List Level 1 List Level 2 List Level 3 List Level 2 List Level 1 ``` produces: 1. List Level 1 1. List Level 2 1. List Level 3 2. List Level 2 2. List Level 1 It is also possible to mix bullet lists and numbered lists. For example: ``` Can I mix definition lists as well? Yes How? It's easy as ABC ``` yields: Can I mix definition lists as well? 1. Yes 2. How? It's easy as ABC When creating lists with multiple paragraphs or elements, special care must be taken to ensure the list structure is maintained. Breaking up a paragraph within a list item can be achieved by using a line break without disrupting the list. For example: ``` This is a list item This is a continuation of the same item. ``` will maintain the list structure. Additionally, a list item can include both a sub-list and further text that is not part of the sub-list. This can be achieved by placing a colon at the appropriate level. However, this method may result in misaligned indentation. For numbered lists that span multiple columns, such as in tables, wiki markup cannot handle this directly. Instead, HTML code must be used to preserve numbering across columns. This approach is unnecessary for bullet-point lists, as numbering is not a concern.
